learning_extracted: A DECOMPOSITION can smuggle in the same non-uniqueness as a transferred BAR, and this run did. The driver's own red-team record kills a transferred bar because 'the equally defensible RESIDUAL transfer implies 0.933 ... and the two give OPPOSITE routes on the authoring seed' -- and then replaces it with a shortfall decomposition that measures the budget factor on `posthoc_ols_r2` while anchoring the gap at `sgd_head_r2`. Substituting the identities, metric_share = 1 - (1 - parity)*pca32/gap, so the criterion fires precisely when the code is near the ceiling AND the SGD head is far below the code -- and the second condition IS head under-training, which is what the budget hypothesis asserts. Both branches are budget; one of them is labelled metric. The general lesson: when a routing rests on shares of a gap, the ORDER in which the factors are removed is a free parameter, and an attribution is only reportable if it is either order-invariant or reported under every ordering. The order-symmetric partition (the standard remedy) is what this autopsy routes on.

The SD-106 preservation term works at its own objective, and this is the part that is ORDER-FREE. Under a post-hoc OLS probe on the same frozen latent, buffer and held-out split the code reaches 0.951 (as-shipped) to 0.980 (at ~3.3x the optimiser steps) of the achievable 32-dim linear ceiling, and beats the paired OFF arm on 3/3 seeds at EVERY budget. `preservation_holdout.r2` is bounded by the head's convergence as well as by the code, so it is a LOWER BOUND on linear-decodable content, never an estimate of it -- and nothing at its emission site says so.

AN EFFECT SIZE MEASURED AT ONE BUDGET IS NOT THE EFFECT SIZE. The mechanism's measured advantage over its own paired control TRIPLES across the swept budget (+0.0169 -> +0.0315 -> +0.0509 median) while the control's own parity stays flat -- so the acceptance measurement that produced the FAIL was taken at roughly one third of the mechanism's within-range effect. The contrast is order-free (a straight paired difference at each budget), which is exactly why it survives the decomposition problem above. Any acceptance measurement of a trained mechanism should report its contrast at more than one training budget, or state that it is reporting a lower bound.

Split 'the budget was too small' into its two coordinates before testing it. Within a 3.3x step range at fixed data and a ~1.7x data range at ~equal steps, the effective coordinate is STEPS: b_steps1200 is best on 3/3 seeds on BOTH statistics, and b_designref -- more data at ~equal steps, the design doc's own reference -- scores below it. The 2x2 is what made this answerable at all.

Reading an encoder-level result onto a consumer-rung shortfall crosses a measurement plane, and the quotient of the two deficits is NOT a ranking of the explanations. A 0.043 held-out world_obs reconstruction-R^2 deficit and a 0.150 oracle-action-agreement deficit are different DVs in different units with no established transfer function; their ratio (~3.5) is a slope estimated from ONE point pair, and a discrete-action decoder can convert a small reconstruction deficit into a large agreement deficit through decision-boundary geometry alone. The first draft of this artifact used that ratio to call a which-directions deficit 'the more economical account' and escalated it in a learning item to 'strong evidence'; BOTH are withdrawn. The legitimate use of the same slope is the opposite one: as the quantified NULL that makes the steep-transfer reading falsifiable by the probe in fanout_recommendation.

The SD-106 design doc's headline figures are not on the P0a observation distribution. PCA-32 of the P0a buffer explains 0.888 of world_obs held-out and 0.893 in-sample on seed 42 (cross-seed held-out median 0.886), against the doc's 0.9983/0.9984 -- a third explanation of the original discrepancy that neither V3-EXQ-1023's autopsy nor its routing named, compounding that autopsy's already-recorded recording gap (no committed producer, so the distribution cannot be recovered from the repo at all).
